name: Southwest Route
rappels: A multi-rappel descent back down the Southwest Arete, mixed with downclimbing, on old in-place anchors that look ancient; back them up. No rappel count is published.
descent_text: There is no walk-off: descend by downclimbing and rappelling the Southwest Arête back toward camp. The in-place rap stations are old fixed and natural anchors (slings around horns and blocks, older bolts or pitons) rather than fresh bolted chains. Plan on a multi-rappel descent down the arête/face using a single 60m rope, re-anchoring at the existing stations, with short downclimbs linking some of the easier sections between rappels — typical Pickets practice on lightly-traveled lines to save time and gear. Because this route sees very few ascents and the fixed anchors are old, inspect every station closely, back it up if there is any doubt, and carry a couple of spare slings/rap rings and cord in case a station needs to be rebuilt or supplemented. From the base of the rock, reverse the talus/scree scramble back to camp in Terror Basin, then retrace the approach: the steep ~2.5 mile / 4,700 ft trail drop to the 'spar tree,' followed by the milder ~4.5 mile climbers' trail back to the Goodell Creek trailhead.
approach: From the Upper Goodell Creek Group Campground trailhead (end of the short Goodell Creek Road spur off the North Cascades Highway near Newhalem, ~600 ft), follow the unmaintained but well-trodden Goodell Creek climbers' trail, which runs along an old overgrown logging road bed paralleling Goodell Creek. The first roughly 4.5 miles are comparatively mellow, mostly forested walking to the old 'spar tree,' where a boot path cut by Seattle Mountaineers work parties continues on. From there the trail turns brutally steep for about 2.5 more miles and 4,700 ft of gain, climbing more or less straight up the timbered nose of ridge between Terror and Crescent Creeks — widely cited as one of the steepest approach trails in the Cascades. The unsigned turn uphill off the old road bed is marked by a large cairn; the path climbs to a notch on the basin rim and drops to the tarns and typical camp in upper Terror Basin below the McMillan-Inspiration wall. Reliable water is available at Goodell Creek crossings low on the trail and at the Terror Basin tarns/snowmelt near camp; carry water above camp, since the final approach onto rock is dry. From camp, angle north/northeast across talus and scree past the small glacial tarn below West McMillan Spire, staying on the McMillan side of the basin (not crossing the Barrier) to reach the base of the southwest arête on Little Mac Spire, the smaller subsidiary spire just east of East McMillan Spire. Expect loose rock, some routefinding through talus and low bluffs, and lingering snow/moat problems at the base of the rock well into summer.
overview: Little Mac Spire is a minor rock pinnacle in the Southern Pickets, immediately adjacent to East McMillan Spire within the McMillan Spires group, North Cascades National Park. It is rarely climbed as a stand-alone objective — most ascents happen when parties already engaged with the McMillan Spires or a full Southern Pickets enchainment tag the summit en route, then continue across to a horn and rappel into the gully below East McMillan Spire. It is reached via the Terror Basin approach from the Goodell Creek trailhead near Newhalem.
beta: The southwest-facing route provides technical alpine climbing with high-quality rock. Approximately 800 feet of climbing to summit with exposed sections requiring careful route-finding.
gear: alpine rock rack (small cams/nuts to ~2 in)
60m rope (for the multi-rappel descent of the arête)
ice axe / microspikes for early-season snow near Terror Basin
